chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from his father, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when Abu Baseer entered, panting heavily. When he took his seat, Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O Abu Muhammad, what is this heavy breathing?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, O son of the Messenger of Allah — great is my age, my bones have become frail, and my appointed time approaches, yet I do not know what I shall encounter from the matters of my Hereafter.'

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Muhammad, are you really saying this?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — how can I not say this?' He said: 'O Abu Muhammad, do you not know that Allah the Most High honours the young ones among you and is bashful toward the elderly?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — how does He honour the young and be bashful toward the elderly?' He said: 'Allah honours the young by not punishing them, and is bashful toward the elderly by not calling them to account.' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — is this exclusively for us or for all the people of Tawhid?' He said: 'No, by Allah, it is exclusively for you (Shia) apart from all the worlds.'

He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — we have been given a name that has broken our backs, killed our hearts, and because of which the rulers have declared our blood permissible to shed, in a hadith narrated to them by their jurists.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Is it al-Rafida (the Rejectors)?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'No, by Allah — it is not they who named you thus; rather, it is Allah Who named you with it.'

Do you not know, O Abu Muhammad, that seventy men from the Children of Israel rejected Pharaoh and his people when his misguidance became clear to them, so they joined Moses (peace be upon him) when his guidance became clear to them? They were called al-Rafida in the army of Moses because they had rejected Pharaoh, and they were the most intense worshippers in that army and the most fervent in their love for Moses, Harun, and their offspring (peace be upon them both). So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Moses (peace be upon him): 'Establish this name for them in the Torah, for I have named them with it and bestowed it upon them.' So Moses (peace be upon him) established the name for them, then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, reserved this name for you until He bestowed it upon you.

O Abu Muhammad — they rejected the good, and you have rejected the evil. All people separated into factions and divided into branches, but you branched out with the People of the Household of your Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family), and you went where they went, and you chose whom Allah chose for you, and you wanted what Allah wanted. So receive glad tidings, then glad tidings again — for by Allah, you are the ones upon whom Allah has mercy; the good deeds of your righteous shall be accepted, and the sins of your wrongdoers shall be overlooked. Whoever does not come before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Judgment with what you are upon, no good deed shall be accepted from him and no sin overlooked. O Abu Muhammad, have I made you happy?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — give me more.'

He said: 'O Abu Muhammad, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has assigned angels to cast sins from the backs of our Shia, just as the wind casts down leaves in the season of their falling. And that is His statement, the Mighty and Majestic: "Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify the praise of their Lord and believe in Him and seek forgiveness for those who believe" [40:7]. By Allah, their seeking forgiveness is for you (Shia) apart from all other creation. O Abu Muhammad, have I made you happy?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — give me more.'

He said: 'O Abu Muhammad, Allah has mentioned you in His Book, saying: "Among the believers are men who have been true to the covenant they made with Allah: some of them have fulfilled their vow, and some are still waiting, and they have not changed in the least" [33:23]. You have been loyal to the covenant Allah took from you concerning our wilayah, and you have not exchanged us for others. Had you not done so, Allah would have reproached you just as He reproached them where He, Majestic is His remembrance, said: "And We did not find in most of them any faithfulness to the covenant, and We found most of them to be transgressors" [7:102]. O Abu Muhammad, have I made you happy?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — give me more.'

He said: 'O Abu Muhammad, Allah has mentioned you in His Book: "as brothers on raised couches, facing one another" [15:47]. By Allah, He intended by this none other than you. O Abu Muhammad, have I made you happy?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — give me more.' He said: 'O Abu Muhammad: "Friends on that Day shall be enemies to one another, except for the God-fearing" [43:67]. By Allah, He intended by this none other than you. O Abu Muhammad, have I made you happy?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — give me more.'

He said: 'O Abu Muhammad, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has mentioned us, our Shia, and our enemies in a verse from His Book. He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: "Are those who know equal to those who do not know? Only those possessed of understanding take heed" [39:9]. We are those who know, our enemies are those who do not know, and our Shia are those possessed of understanding. O Abu Muhammad, have I made you happy?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — give me more.'

He said: 'O Abu Muhammad, by Allah, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has made no exception for any of the successors of the prophets nor their followers except for Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) and his Shia. He said in His Book, and His word is truth: "A day when no patron shall avail a patron anything, nor shall they be helped — except those upon whom Allah shall have mercy" [44:41-42], meaning by that Ali (peace be upon him) and his Shia. O Abu Muhammad, have I made you happy?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — give me more.'

He said: 'O Abu Muhammad, Allah the Most High has mentioned you when He said: "O My servants who have exceeded against themselves — do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins; indeed He is the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful" [39:53]. By Allah, He intended by this none other than you. Have I made you happy, O Abu Muhammad?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — give me more.'

He said: 'O Abu Muhammad, Allah has mentioned you in His Book: "Indeed, My servants — you have no authority over them; and your Lord is sufficient as a Protector" [17:65]. By Allah, He intended by this none other than the Imams (peace be upon them) and their Shia. Have I made you happy, O Abu Muhammad?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — give me more.'

He said: 'O Abu Muhammad, Allah has mentioned you in His Book: "Those shall be with those upon whom Allah has bestowed His favour — from among the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous — and excellent are those as companions" [4:69]. So the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) is in the verse the Prophet, and we in this position are the truthful and the martyrs, and you are the righteous — so call yourselves by righteousness as Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has named you. O Abu Muhammad, have I made you happy?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — give me more.'

He said: 'O Abu Muhammad, Allah has mentioned you when He narrated what your enemies will say in the Fire: "And they said: What is the matter with us — we do not see men whom we used to count among the wicked. Did we take them in scorn, or have our eyes turned away from them?" [38:62-63]. By Allah, He meant and intended by this none other than you. You have become in the eyes of the people of this world the worst of people, but by Allah, you shall be delighted in Paradise while you are sought for in the Fire. O Abu Muhammad, have I made you happy?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — give me more.'

He said: 'O Abu Muhammad, there is no verse revealed that leads to Paradise and mentions its people with goodness except that it is about us and our Shia; and there is no verse revealed that mentions its people with evil or points toward the Fire except that it is about our enemies and those who oppose us. Have I made you happy, O Abu Muhammad?' He said: 'May I be sacrificed for you — give me more.' He said: 'O Abu Muhammad, no one is upon the religion of Ibrahim except us and our Shia, while all other people are far removed from that. O Abu Muhammad, have I made you happy?' And in another narration, he said: 'That is enough.'

key_terms.الرَّافِضَة: Al-Rafida — a term applied pejoratively to Shia Muslims, here reframed by the Imam as a divinely-assigned honorable name, tracing its origin to the seventy Israelites who rejected Pharaoh
key_terms.الشَّبَاب: The young ones — those young in faith among the Shia
key_terms.الشِّيعَة: The Shia — followers of the Ahlulbayt who maintain their covenant
key_terms.الْكُهُول: The elderly/mature ones — those advanced in age among the Shia
key_terms.الْوَلَايَة: Wilayah — the covenant of guardianship and authority of the Imams

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the divine mercy granted to the Shia, and what is the origin of the name al-Rafida?
ai.summary: This hadith records a private conversation between Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and his elderly companion Abu Baseer (Abu Muhammad Yahya al-Asswari), who was distressed about his approaching death and uncertain about his hereafter. The Imam reassures him with twelve successive consolations, each citing divine mercy, Quranic references, or historical precedents to affirm the elevated spiritual status of the Shia — those who maintain the wilayah of the Ahlulbayt. The dialogue exemplifies the pastoral role of the Imam in comforting and spiritually anchoring his close companions, taking place during the Umayyad/early Abbasid period when Shia faced severe political persecution and were labeled 'al-Rafida' (the Rejectors) to justify violence against them.

He (azwj) Said: “[4:69] these are with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favours from among the prophets and the truthful and the martyrs and the righteous, and a goodly company are they!” So the Messenger (saww) of Allah (azwj) in the Verse is ‘from among the Prophets (as)’, and we (a.s.), in this subject are the ‘truthful and the martyrs’, and you all are the ‘righteous’, therefore adopt this name by the righteousness as Allah (azwj) Mighty and Majestic has Named you. O Abu Muhammad, so, have I made you happy?’ He said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you (a.s.), increase it for me’.

He (a.s.) said: ‘O Abu Muhammad, Allah (azwj) has Mentioned you all when He (azwj) Narrated about your enemies in the Fire by His (azwj) Statement: “[38:62] And they shall say: What is the matter with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the vicious? [38:63] Was it that we (only) took them in scorn, or have our eyes (now) turned aside from them?” And Allah (azwj) has not Meant, and not Intended by this other than you (Shiites). You have become as the evil people in the eyes of this world, and by Allah (azwj), you will be in the Paradise you will be in delight whereas in the Fire you will be sought. O Abu Muhammad, so have I (a.s.) made you happy?’ He said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you (a.s.), increase it for me’.

He (a.s.) said: ‘O Abu Muhammad, there is none from the Verses Revealed Which Guides to the Paradise, nor Mentions it addressees with goodness except that it is regarding us (a.s.) and regarding our (a.s.) Shiites. And there is none from the Verses Revealed Which Mentions its addressees with evil, or Points to the Fire except that it is regarding our (a.s.) enemies and the ones who are opposed to us (a.s.). So, have I (a.s.) made you happy, O Abu Muhammad?’ He said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you (a.s.), increase it for me’. So he (a.s.) said: ‘O Abu Muhammad, There is no one upon the Nation of Ibrahim (as) except for us (a.s.), and our (a.s.) Shiites, whereas the rest of the people are remote from that. O Abu Muhammad, have I (a.s.) made you happy?’ And in another report, he (a.s.) said: ‘This is enough’.
